title: Panzanella Salad With Duck Bacon
description: Sweet and glistening Sun Gold tomatoes contrast the deep earthy notes of sourdough or pumpernickel bread in this peak-season salad. Toss the bread cubes with rendered bacon fat before toasting for an added layer of smokiness. A simple sherry vinaigrette gets a double dose of tomato flavor from hand-crushed Sun Golds and fresh tomato juice.
ingredients: 8 duck (or regular) bacon slices, cut into 3-inch pieces (about 10 ounces)
12 cups cubed (about 1-inch pieces) pumpernickel or sourdough bread (about 1 pound)
7 cups cherry tomatoes (about 2 1/4 pounds), preferably Sun Gold or a mixture, halved
1 cup loosely packed fresh basil leaves, plus more for garnish
1 red bell pepper stemmed, seeded, and thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
directions: Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium, stirring often, until crispy and fat has rendered, 10 to 12 minutes. Transfer bacon to a paper towel–lined plate; set aside.

Pour 1/4 cup rendered bacon fat into a large heatproof bowl. Add bread cubes to bowl, and toss to coat. Spread bread in a single layer on prepared baking sheet, reserving large bowl. Bake bread until crispy, about 15 minutes. Let cool on baking sheet 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss together tomatoes and 2 teaspoons salt in a colander over reserved bowl. Let stand until about 1/4 cup tomato juice has drained into bowl, about 15 minutes.

Add 1 cup tomatoes to juices, and coarsely crush using your hands or a potato masher. Whisk in vinegar, mustard, honey, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Gradually whisk in oil until combined.
Add basil, bell pepper, onion, bacon, bread cubes, remaining tomatoes, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon black pepper to vinaigrette in bowl; toss gently to combine.
Garnish with basil leaves, and serve immediately.
